Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

flexyBayes 0.6.0

New features

  • flexybayes_stream() fits mixed models to out-of-core datasets by streaming exact aggregation. The data is read in row-range chunks from an .fst file, a vector of partitioned .fst shards, a delimited file, an in-memory frame, or a chunk-generator function; per-cell sufficient statistics are accumulated additively across chunks and never expanded back to the full row count. Peak memory is bounded by one chunk plus the cell accumulator, not by the row count, so a replicated factorial design fits at hundreds of millions to a billion rows through the same footprint as a small one.
  • The aggregated likelihood is exact for the gaussian, binomial, and poisson families. Summing within a cell preserves the likelihood (gaussian sum of squares; binomial successes / trials; poisson counts / exposure), so the fitted posterior is the full-data posterior, not an approximation. The streaming path fits through inla or greta.
  • Out-of-scope models are refused before any data is read. Continuous fixed covariates (one cell per row), random slopes, structured covariance, and smooth terms break the cell-constant linear predictor and are refused with a named reason code rather than silently approximated.
  • In-memory flexybayes(aggregate = ) now aggregates binomial and poisson, not only gaussian. A 0/1 binomial or a poisson model with a factor cell key and a productive compression routes through the exact count aggregation under aggregate = "auto" / TRUE; the dispatch trace reads path == "aggregated_count". Non-Bernoulli binomial responses and weighted count models fall through to the per-row path.

flexyBayes 0.5.0

The verb surface, finalised (breaking change)

The fitting surface now has one consistent shape: a universal entry that spans every backend, single-engine pins, and exported ingest adapters. The deprecation windows opened at 0.4.1 are now closed.

  • Engine pins are single-engine, by name. fb_greta(), fb_inla(), and fb_brms() each fit via exactly one engine — fb_<engine>(...) is sugar for fb(..., backend = "<engine>"). Passing a conflicting backend to a pin is now a clear error rather than being silently overridden. fb_brms(backend = "brms") (the redundant self-pin) is still accepted.
  • fb_brms() no longer takes a non-brms backend. The multi-backend role moved to fb() / flexybayes() at 0.4.1; at 0.5.0 fb_brms() is the brms engine pin. Pass the same formula to fb() to reach greta, inla, or auto.
  • fb() / flexybayes() fit a native greta model directly. Pass a greta::model() object (or a fb_from_greta() intermediate representation) straight to fb(); it is fit via greta and returned with the full post-fit surface. To keep a canonical-name map for cross-engine triangulate(), build the representation once and reuse it: fb(fb_from_greta(model, canonical_names = c(...))).
  • fb_greta(model = ) is no longer a separate native-graph verb. The model = argument still works (it is mapped to the universal model slot), so existing native-graph calls keep fitting; the recommended form is fb_greta(model) or, with a canonical map, fb_greta(fb_from_greta(model, canonical_names = c(...))).

Backend selection has one home

Backend availability, per-engine capability, and the auto candidate set are all sourced from a single locked registry, so an unsupported (model x engine) pair always yields a registered, structured refusal naming the offending construct.

Bug fixes

  • triangulate() now compares INLA variance components on the standard- deviation scale. The automatic precision-to-standard-deviation conversion for an INLA fit was keyed so that it silently did not fire, so a cross-engine comparison (for example greta versus INLA) reported the INLA precision against the other engine’s standard deviation on the sigma and sd_<group> rows. The conversion now fires by default, with no need to pass transform_b by hand.
  • plot() works on every backend fit. Previously only a greta fit had a plot() method, so plot() on an INLA, brms, aggregated, or native-greta fit fell through to graphics::plot.default() and errored. plot(fit, type = "effects") now works on any backend, and plot types that need quantities a backend does not expose (trace plots without MCMC draws, residual plots without fitted values) report that clearly instead of erroring.
  • Positional and named prior arguments behave identically. A prior written positionally (for example normal(0, 50)) is now read the same as the named form (normal(0, sd = 50)) on every emit path; previously a positional scale could be silently dropped to the default on the greta and INLA paths.
  • predict(), emmeans(), and marginaleffects work on an INLA fit of a brms-grammar mixed model. A model written as y ~ x + (1 | g) and fitted via INLA previously refused these downstream calls, because the random-effect bar term leaked into the fixed-effect design matrix. formula() on an INLA fit now returns the fixed-effect formula only, as documented, so the design matrix matches the fitted coefficients. Aggregated INLA fits are covered too.
  • A non-binary binomial response is refused on the greta backend rather than being silently fitted as a Bernoulli model.
  • Internal faults are no longer swallowed. A genuine fault in the latent-Gaussian gate during aggregated auto routing, and a failure to compute logLik(), now surface rather than being silently turned into a fallback or NA.

flexyBayes 0.4.1

One universal entry across every grammar and backend

fb() / flexybayes() becomes the single entry for any input grammar and any backend, with single-engine pins alongside it.

  • Grammar polymorphism. fb() / flexybayes() now accept a brms / lme4-style bar-grouped formula (response ~ x + (1 | g)) in addition to the ASReml fixed / random / rcov form. The grammar is detected from the call shape; the new syntax argument forces it. A brms-style model now reaches every available backend through the universal entry, not just one.
  • Engine pins. fb_inla() joins fb_greta() as a single-engine fitting verb: fb_inla(...) is exactly fb(..., backend = "inla"), and accepts the same grammars.
  • Exported ingest adapters. fb_from_asreml(), fb_from_brms() and fb_from_greta() are now exported. They turn a model specification into the backend-agnostic intermediate representation, for inspection, caching, or hand-off to a fitting verb.
  • Registry-driven backend selection. Backend availability, capability, and the auto candidate set are sourced from a single locked backend registry, so the dispatch facts have one home.

Deprecations

  • fb_brms() with a non-brms backend is deprecated. Pass the same formula to fb() / flexybayes(), which now detects brms grammar and reaches every backend (including the same auto / greta / inla routing). fb_brms(backend = "brms") is unaffected. The multi-backend form is removed at 0.5.0, when fb_brms() becomes the brms engine pin.
  • The fb_greta(model = ) native-graph signature is deprecated. Build the intermediate representation from a native greta model with fb_from_greta(). The signature is removed at 0.5.0, when fb_greta() becomes the greta engine pin.

flexyBayes 0.4.0

Covariance carriers: the fb_cov() constructor (breaking change)

Structured covariance is now declared with the fb_cov() constructor noun inside a random term, completing the four-constructor surface (fb_prior(), fb_engine(), fb_approx(), fb_cov()).

  • fb_cov(M, type) wraps a covariance carrier and is passed via the cov argument: vm(geno, cov = fb_cov(L, type = "chol")). The five carrier types are "dense", "chol", "precision", "blocks", and "low_rank" (the last is a reserved vocabulary entry at this release). The constructor returns a classed object carrying its representation_class and a construction-time validation_summary; it comes with is_fb_cov() and a print method.
  • The legacy vm() / ped() keyword carriers are deprecated. The four forms introduced in v0.3.7 — vm(group, chol = L), vm(group, precision = Q), vm(group, blocks = list(...)), and vm(group, low_rank_factor = U, low_rank_scheme = "pca") — now emit a lifecycle migration warning naming the fb_cov() replacement. They continue to work in 0.4.0 and will be removed at 0.5.0. The bare dense forms vm(group, V) / ped(group, A) are unchanged.

New constructor nouns: fb_engine() and fb_approx()

Two named constructors join fb_prior(), so a model’s inference engine and any approximation are specified as explicit, printable objects rather than bare strings.

  • fb_engine(name, opts) names an inference engine ("greta", "inla", "brms") and its sampler tuning, and is passed as the backend argument: flexybayes(..., backend = fb_engine("greta", chains = 4L)). It records the engine’s inference paradigm and a toolchain_status reflecting whether the engine’s package is installed. The bare-string form (backend = "greta") continues to work unchanged.
  • fb_approx(scheme, ...) names an approximation scheme — validated against the approximation registry — and its tuning, and is passed as a smooth representation: s(x, representation = fb_approx("low_rank_smooth", rank = 5L)). It carries a literature-referenced description of the scheme’s bias bound. An unregistered scheme is refused with the supported vocabulary.
  • Both come with is_fb_engine() / is_fb_approx() predicates and print methods.

emmeans and marginaleffects now work end-to-end

Fits now expose the standard model interface that the downstream estimation ecosystem dispatches on, so estimated marginal means, contrasts, predictions, slopes, and comparisons work directly on both the greta and INLA backends.

  • emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ f) and contrast() work on greta- and INLA-backed fits. The estimation basis is built to match each backend’s fixed-effect parametrisation — treatment contrasts on INLA, the over-parameterised (intercept + all factor levels) basis on greta, the latter handled through a non-estimability basis so only estimable combinations are reported. Posterior summaries use z-intervals.
  • marginaleffects::predictions(), avg_slopes(), and avg_comparisons() work on both backends via the get_coef() / set_coef() / get_vcov() / get_predict() accessors, with population-level (fixed-effect) predictions on the identity link.
  • Per-row INLA fits gain coef(), vcov(), predict(), formula(), and family() methods. vcov() returns a Monte-Carlo estimate of the joint posterior covariance of the fixed effects (its marginal standard deviations match the INLA fixed-effect summary); predict(newdata = ...) returns fixed-effect predictions.
  • A model whose fixed-effect design cannot be reconciled one-to-one with its fitted coefficients is refused with a clear message pointing to the posterior-draws workflow, rather than silently mis-mapped.

Triangulation now labels its convergence claim by independence axis

triangulate() reports gain an independence axis label, so a cross-engine agreement says what kind of convergence it is, not just how close. A small distance between two HMC fits (“implementation” independence) underwrites a weaker claim than the same distance between an HMC fit and a Laplace-approximation fit (“algorithmic” independence).

  • Every triangulate() result carries independence (a vector from the closed vocabulary algorithmic / implementation / specification) and axis_justification (a one-line explanation). The print method surfaces the label, colour-graded by methodological strength on a colour terminal (plain text everywhere else). The Wasserstein columns are unchanged, so existing consumers keep working. The label follows Gelman et al. (2020, Bayesian Workflow, arXiv:2011.01808) §6 on cross-checks across implementations.
  • The three v0.3.x backend pairs (greta–inla, greta–brms, brms–inla) are labelled; same-backend or unregistered pairs render without the label rather than refusing.

Aggregated triangulation and matched-prior transparency

  • triangulate() now works on greta-aggregated fits. Aggregated greta fits previously did not expose their posterior draws in the layout the draw extractor expects, so triangulate(), canonical_names(), confint(), plot(), and predict() failed on them; they now work.
  • Aggregated-gaussian fits report their prior parametrization. A new prior_parametrization field ("per_row_equivalent" under the default precision prior, "custom" otherwise) is shown in the aggregated print() / summary() and returned by canonical_names(), so it is clear whether the aggregated posterior matches the per-row posterior.
  • triangulate() documents the matched-prior caveat for aggregated inputs, forward-linking prior_summary().

fb_refusals() — a browsable registry of refusal reasons

flexyBayes now ships a complete, locked vocabulary of the conditions under which it declines to fit, route, or validate a model, exposed through a new exported accessor and a precise condition-class contract.

  • New exported function fb_refusals(reason_code = NULL, since_version = NULL). Returns an fb_refusals_table data frame — one row per refusal reason carrying its reason_code, a one-line description, the since_version it was introduced in, and the related plan_field — with a compact print method. Optional filters narrow the listing to specific reason codes or to an introducing-version prefix (fb_refusals(since_version = "0.4")).
  • Precise, catchable refusal classes. Every user-facing refusal now carries a condition class flexybayes_refusal_<reason_code> above its existing family class, so a specific refusal can be caught directly, for example tryCatch(fit, flexybayes_refusal_precision_not_symmetric = handler). The registry holds the complete 39-reason vocabulary; routing-decision reasons and internal control-flow signals are deliberately excluded as they are not refusals a user can encounter.
  • The aggregated-emit out-of-scope refusal’s reason code is now rcov_type_unsupported_for_aggregation (previously a less descriptive identifier).
  • Unsupported families now refuse through the registry. Requesting a family flexyBayes cannot fit — for example a survival / time-to-event likelihood — is declined at the family gate with the catchable unsupported_family refusal, which lists the supported families and points to fb_refusals().
  • Parse-time spec refusals now route through the registry. Early formula checks raise catchable refusals instead of bare errors: a one-sided formula (formula_not_two_sided), a response absent from data (response_not_in_data), a factor-analytic rank below one (fa_rank_invalid), and a smooth variable absent from data (smooth_variable_not_in_data). The review_code / return_code entry-point guards likewise raise catchable refusals (review_code_backend_unsupported, code_flags_mutually_exclusive).
  • Tensor-product smooths are now refused, not silently accepted. te(), ti(), and t2() raise tensor_smooth_unsupported rather than being parsed as ordinary named terms; flexyBayes fits univariate penalised splines (s(), spl()) only. The README gains a Known limitations section documenting the spatial (AR1-only), smooth (univariate-only), survival / HMM (deferred), and missing-data scope boundaries.

validate_approximation() + the low_rank_smooth smooth approximation

Completes the approximation contract end to end: the low_rank_smooth scheme, its greta emit path, and the exported validate_approximation() verb land together so every registered scheme carries a working validation procedure.

  • New exported verb validate_approximation(fit, threshold = 0.99) — the sixth (and architecturally-final) exported verb. Returns an <fb_approximation_validation> object reporting, per approximated smooth, the realised Frobenius capture () against the pass threshold (default 0.99), the overall pass / fail verdict, and a fallback hint. An exact fit refuses (approximation_scheme_unknown).
  • low_rank_smooth approximation scheme. Request a rank-K principal-component truncation of a smooth basis with s(x, representation = list(scheme = "low_rank_smooth", rank = K)). The model then carries K basis coefficients (the truncated basis B_K = B V_K, with V_K the top-K right singular vectors of the basis B) instead of the full k; prediction projects the newdata basis through the same V_K. The rank refuses unless it is a positive integer no greater than min(basis dimension, n).
  • Three-tier exactness vocabulary — exact, aggregated_exact, and approximate_<scheme>. Approximate fits carry an [APPROX: <scheme>] badge on the Representation: print line and in fb_plan(); every pre-existing fit’s label is unchanged.
  • Greta backend only. low_rank_smooth truncates the dense mgcv smooth basis, which only the greta backend materialises; an explicit backend = "inla" or "brms" request for a low-rank smooth refuses (low_rank_requires_greta) rather than silently fitting a different smooth representation, and backend = "auto" resolves to greta.
  • Representation registry gains the low_rank class (sixteenth entry).
  • Fix: the brms-formula ingest’s unsupported-feature refusal no longer errors on a multi-line deparse(); a long unsupported term now surfaces the intended clean refusal.

C5 approximation-registry scaffold (ADR 0030 + ADR 0027, v0.4.0 Wave 1 Phase 1A substrate)

Ships the approximation-scheme registry infrastructure — a single locked .approximation_registry environment populated at .onLoad() and locked via .lock_approximation_registry(), with the .register_approximation() (five-field ADR 0027 Decision 2 schema: scheme, bias_bound, validation_fn, fallback_hint, registered_in_adr), .lookup_approximation(), and .approximation_scheme() helpers. Empty at this step by design.

  • The container ships ahead of its first scheme, mirroring the v0.3.8 C7 refusal-registry scaffold (container at v0.3.8, first population at v0.3.10). The first approximation scheme (low_rank_smooth) registers together with its emit path and the exported validate_approximation() surface, because the scheme’s validation_fn reads the truncated and full smooth-basis matrices off a fit object that only the emit path produces; landing the scheme, its validation procedure, and its producer in one end-to-end-verifiable change honours the registry invariant that every registered scheme carries a working validation procedure.
  • No user-facing API change at this step. validate_approximation(), the low_rank_smooth scheme, the [APPROX: <scheme>] print badge, and the three-tier exactness controlled vocabulary land in the Phase 1B completion change.
  • Nine acceptance criteria in tests/testthat/test-approximation-registry.R (container exists + locked; empty at the scaffold step; five-field input validation; locked-registry refusal; unknown-scheme refusal with the empty-vocabulary hint; non-string-input refusal; .approximation_scheme() refusal delegation; user-side assign() raises; empty-vocabulary snapshot for vocab-lock gating).

C4 representation registry formalised (ADR 0030, v0.4.0 Wave 1 Phase 1A)

Phase 1A ratifies ADR 0030 contract C4 (closed-vocabulary representation classes) end-to-end. The representation-class vocabulary previously spread informally across R/fb_preflight.R, R/fb_plan.R, and R/methods_truth_display.R as inline string literals now lives in a single locked .representation_registry environment populated at .onLoad() and locked immediately after via .lock_representation_registry(). Consumer sites route every reference through .representation_class("<name>"), so typos refuse at runtime rather than silently propagating an unknown class through preflight / planning / display.

  • Fifteen entries at v0.4.0 open: the ten plan-named classes (dense_cov, chol_cov, sparse_precision, pedigree_sparse_precision, block_diagonal, dense_smooth, sparse_smooth, banded_smooth, indexed_structured_known, indexed_structured_estimate) plus five additional classes load-bearing in the v0.3.10 source and surfaced during the Phase 1A producer-site sweep (indexed_random_intercept, dense_baseline, indexed_fixed_numeric, indexed_fixed_factor, indexed_fixed_factor_numeric). low_rank registers in Phase 1B alongside the ADR 0027 approximation registry; the axis_* reservation lands in Phase 2B with the backend-independence axis vocabulary.
  • Internal helpers: .register_representation(name, description, category, registered_in_adr, since_version) validates inputs, refuses duplicate names, and refuses any attempt to register after the registry locks. .lookup_representation(name) returns the full registered entry and refuses unknown names with the known-classes hint. .representation_class(name) is the edit-light thin wrapper consumer sites call to swap a bare string literal for a validated-name round-trip.
  • Twelve acceptance criteria in tests/testthat/test-representation-registry.R (container exists + locked, vocabulary completeness, schema check on every entry, lookup round-trip, lookup refusal on unknown name + non-string input, .representation_class() round-trip, registration input validation, duplicate refusal, locked-registry refusal, user-side assign() raises, vocabulary snapshot for vocab-lock gating). The snapshot test forces every future vocabulary addition or removal through a conscious maintainer-review step rather than silently mutating the registry.
  • No user-facing API change. Refusal messages on unknown representation classes surface earlier (at .representation_class() instead of at the consumer site downstream) but carry identical content; existing tests that assert specific refusal messages continue to pass.

flexyBayes 0.3.10

Stage 5A blocks emit + low_rank refusal-stub upgrade (ADR 0025 Decisions 3 + 4)

Phase A closes two of the three v0.3.8-deferred items that v0.3.9 did not absorb. The block-diagonal carrier vm(group, blocks = ...) ships end-to-end on greta + INLA; the low-rank refusal upgrades to name the v0.4.0 validate_approximation() forward export by reference, and three new reason codes register into the v0.3.8 C7 refusal-registry scaffold as the first migration (forward-pattern demonstration for the v0.4.0 Wave 1 Phase 1C bulk migration).

  • vm(group, blocks = my_blocks) — where my_blocks resolves to list(V_1, ..., V_K) — is active on greta + INLA. The greta path emits via t(chol(as.matrix(Matrix::bdiag(...)))) through .vm_ped_sqrt_expr() (fits the v0.3.7 sqrt-expr architecture unchanged; “exact and boring” per the 2026-05-28 planning correction). The INLA path emits K independent f(<var>_id_block_<k>, model = "generic0", Cmatrix = solve(V_k)) calls; per-block integer index columns + per-block precision matrices are pre-computed in data_inla.
  • vm(group, low_rank_factor = U, low_rank_scheme = "pca") refuses with the upgraded message naming ADR 0027 + validate_approximation() (v0.4.0 Wave 1 Phase 1B) and the actionable workaround vm(group, V = U %*% t(U)) for the dense materialisation path.
  • Two new structured refusals: block_partition_incomplete (sum of block sizes does not match the grouping factor’s level count) and block_not_positive_definite (offending block index named in the message text).
  • fb_plan() reports representation_plan entries with class block_diagonal for blocks-format vm/ped terms; the print form renders (K blocks) annotations from known_matrices resolution. The fit-side print.flexybayes() Representation line renders exact (block-diagonal, K blocks) when blocks-format terms are present.
  • lgm_gate() check 8 (random_term_type_inla) accepts vm/ped with cov_representation$format == "blocks"; the refusal text for format %in% c("dense", "chol") extends to mention the blocks carrier as a third structurally-INLA-eligible representation.
  • The refusal-registry scaffold (ADR 0030 C7, shipped at v0.3.8 with zero entries) gains its first three entries via .populate_refusal_registry_v0310() — registered at .onLoad() before the registry locks. The full ~28-site migration follows the same .register_refusal() shape at v0.4.0 Wave 1 Phase 1C.

Per-term INLA memory estimator (ADR 0024 §Consequences amendments (a) + (c))

Phase B replaces the v0.3.6 single-multiplier INLA memory check with a per-term decomposition keyed on representation class.

  • <fb_preflight> gains a memory_estimate slot carrying an <fb_memory_estimate> carrier with $total (bytes after the INLA overhead constant; default 2x; configurable via flexyBayes.preflight_inla_overhead_factor), $breakdown (a stable-shape data.frame with rows term_label, representation, bytes, share — ADR 0030 §C4 closed-vocabulary discipline), and the pre-overhead $raw_total. as.numeric(pf$memory_estimate) returns the total, so existing scalar-numeric consumers keep working unchanged.
  • lgm_gate() rule 11 (memory_feasibility_inla) decomposes per term when memory_estimate is present: dense n^2, sparse precision nnz(Q) * 16 (per Lindgren et al. 2011), block-diagonal sum_k n_k^2 * 8, indexed random 8K + 4N, fixed effects N * p * 8. Refuses with the new reason code memory_feasibility_inla_per_term and names the largest contributor + its representation on the diagnostic line.
  • fb_plan() print form renders the breakdown rows under the headline memory line: total + overhead factor followed by one indented row per term with representation class + bytes.
  • New vignette flexyBayes-13-lgm-feasibility-memory walks through the per-term model, how to read memory_estimate$breakdown, four patterns to negotiate a refusal, and the SPDE-mesh / approximate- scheme surfaces explicitly out of scope at v0.3.10.

flexyBayes 0.3.9

Test-isolation pass – three v0.3.8-deferred stochastic flakes closed

Four themed Phase commits close the three v0.3.8-deferred stochastic flakes (test-smooth.R:88, test-validation-lmer.R:31, test-emit-gaussian-aggregated.R:299) and consolidate the test- isolation contract under a single-call umbrella. The [flake-test-infrastructure] and [flake-stochastic-rng] classes in inst/skip-ledger.md drop to zero residual entries; the replacement entries under the Stress-only class are opt-in via FLEXYBAYES_RUN_STRESS=true by design.

Phase A fix: (emit-state latch encapsulation + bare-options leak repair).

  • The once-per-session message latches (default-prior note, uniform-on-INLA approx note) migrate from the options() namespace into a package-private environment in R/emit_state.R. Accessors .emit_state_get / .emit_state_set / .init_emit_state keep the state invisible to user code; the public-API options(flexyBayes.silence_*) toggles are unchanged. Test isolation gets a withr-scoped helper at tests/testthat/helper-emit-state.R; the regression suite at tests/testthat/test-emit-state-isolation.R pins the contract in 15 expectations across 7 test_that blocks.
  • Six bare options(flexyBayes.silence_default_prior_note = TRUE) calls (one in test-inla-verification-simple-slope-uncor.R, five in test-random-slopes-uncor.R) migrate to withr::local_options() so the silence flag does not leak across files in tools/tally.R’s single-process loop. Bisection during Phase A traced the v0.3.8 flake at test-smooth.R:88 through the env migration to this leak as the upstream cause; either fix alone is insufficient.

Phase B fix: (TF-RNG containment + hybrid sleepstudy validation).

  • New test helper tests/testthat/helper-rng.R exposes local_tf_seed(seed, .local_envir, deterministic_ops = FALSE) which reseeds both R (set.seed) and TensorFlow (tf$random$set_seed via requireNamespace("tensorflow")); deterministic_ops = TRUE additionally enables tf$config$experimental$enable_op_determinism() (opt-in; process-global state + 5–15% throughput cost).
  • The sleepstudy flexybayes()-vs-lme4 validation test (test-validation-lmer.R:31) splits into a hybrid: primary always-on path at 1000+1000 budget + 1.5 * REML SE fixed-effect tolerance + 30% VC tolerance; secondary stress-gated path at 2000+2000 + 1.0 * REML SE / 25% (the original strict assertion). Both paths call local_tf_seed(20260427L) at entry. The stress-gated companion joins the existing stress- only blocks under tools/profiles/stress.R.

Phase B’ fix: (aggregated INLA bit-exact identity tolerance amendment).

  • The INLA per-row + aggregated agree on beta assertion (test-emit-gaussian-aggregated.R:284) splits: always-on band at 5e-3 (10x the spike’s 1e-4 theoretical bit-exact claim, 1.5x the v0.3.8 Phase D worst-case observation of 3.4e-3) with a stress-gated companion at the original 1e-3 floor. Same shape as the v0.3.5 BLAS-non-associativity amendment on ADR 0023 and the v0.3.7 subtest (d) loosening on ADR 0025; the algebraic-identity claim documented at R/emit_gaussian_aggregated.R:30-41 is unchanged.

Phase C feat: (single-call test-isolation umbrella).

  • New helper tests/testthat/helper-isolation.R exposes local_flexybayes_clean_state(seed = NULL, .local_envir, deterministic_ops = FALSE) that composes local_clean_emit_state() unconditionally and local_tf_seed() when a seed is provided. The umbrella file header consolidates the three cross-helper discipline rules learned during Phase A + B + B’: never bare options(flexyBayes.*) without withr::local_options(); greta-MCMC numerical- agreement tests must call local_tf_seed(); emit-state- dependent tests must call local_clean_emit_state(). Each underlying helper remains the right entry point for single- surface tests.

User-facing impact: zero. All changes are test-infrastructure or test-tolerance only. Public-API options(flexyBayes.silence_*) toggles unchanged. flexybayes() / fb_brms() / fb_plan() signatures unchanged. The internal flexyBayes._..._emitted option names (leading-underscore, never declared API) are no longer consulted by package code.

Cumulative tally on the v0.3.9 release tree: PASS 1894 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 8 (was 1871 / 0 / 8 at v0.3.8; +23 PASS, equal SKIP count). The skip-count parity is intentional – each closed flake-class skip is replaced by an opt-in stress-gated skip exercising the strict assertion under the release-rehearsal probe.

flexyBayes 0.3.8

Audit-close hardening + planner + truth display

Four themed Phase commits close the 2026-05-25 audit (feedback_v0.3.7_to_v0.4.0_2026-05-25.md, five Critical Fixes and thirteen sub-recommendations) and ratify ADR 0030 contracts C1 (planner verb) + C7 (refusal-registry scaffold) + Decision 4 (Representation: / Engine: two-line truth display).

Phase A fix: (shared prediction kernel + alignment validators + sparse-precision policy).

  • File-backed prediction and the in-memory path now share a single per-draw kernel (R/predict_kernel.R); the smooth-bypass bug on predict(..., output_file = ...) that lost partial contributions of spline terms is closed. Audit Critical Fix #1.
  • Known-matrix carriers passed via known_matrices = list(...) validate against the IR at fit time on both backends: dimension mismatches, level mismatches between dimnames(M) and the factor’s levels(), and dimname misalignments raise typed refusals (known_matrix_dim_mismatch, known_matrix_dimnames_mismatch, known_matrix_level_mismatch) instead of crashing inside the emit. Audit Critical Fix #2.
  • The PD probe on user-supplied sparse precision matrices Q is now sparse-native – Matrix::chol(forceSymmetric(Q)) rather than coercing to dense and calling base chol(). The flexyBayes.trust_pd option allows callers who have already verified PD externally to skip the probe. Audit Critical Fix #3.

Phase B feat: (planner + truth display + refusal registry scaffold).

  • New exported verb fb_plan(formula, data, backend, priors, known_matrices, family, link, weights, aggregate, memory_ceiling_gb, predict_plan, ...). Returns a <fb_plan> object showing the pre-fit dispatch decision, representation plan, rejected-route trace, predict-shape derivation, and known-matrix summary – without running the fit. print() surfaces a flight-checklist form; summary() adds per-term preflight detail; as.data.frame() coerces to a wide single row for tabular aggregation across plans. flexybayes() and fb_brms() accept plan = FALSE (default) -> TRUE to short-circuit to the plan. ADR 0030 contract C1.
  • print.flexybayes() / summary.flexybayes() / print.flexybayes_aggregated() replace the single Exact.: line with two adjacent lines Representation: (the IR’s exactness vocabulary – exact_index, aggregated_exact, legacy_inla_simple_slope, etc.) and Engine: (the live engine name – greta_MCMC, INLA_Laplace, stan_brms_HMC – distinct from Representation: because several representations can run on the same engine). Closes audit Critical Fix #4. ADR 0030 Decision 4.
  • New .refusal_registry environment + .register_refusal() / .lookup_refusal() helpers, empty + locked at end of .onLoad(). Per-site migration of the ~30 existing stop() refusals to registry-backed messages is deferred to v0.4.0 per feedback_staged_release_pattern; the v0.3.8 scaffold is forward-architecture for the v0.4.0 export of fb_refusals(). ADR 0030 contract C7.

Phase C docs: (audit-drift close + selective vignette refresh).

  • Workspace AGENTS.md rewritten as a thin pointer to CLAUDE.md (eliminates the stale bayesreml / Codex (ctb) references the audit flagged).
  • Workspace README.md replaced (the 2026-04-26 pre-implementation review guide is now historical; current-state README documents v0.2.5 -> v0.3.7 release history + the local-tarball install path pending D8).
  • Package README.md: install line replaces the 404-ing remotes::install_github("AAGI-AUS/flexyBayes") with R CMD INSTALL release_tarballs/flexyBayes_0.3.8.tar.gz plus a “will resume after D8” forward-pointer.
  • AMBITION_STAGE.md §8.6: v0.3.6 mis-label corrected (Stage 4 ADR 0024, not Stage 5B ADR 0026); v0.3.7 + v0.3.8 rows added.
  • ADR 0024 §Consequences amendments (a) per-term INLA estimator
      1. vignette companion both updated to reflect the v0.3.7 -> v0.3.8 -> follow-on deferral chain.
  • Selective vignette re-precompile – only vignettes whose printed code chunks render print(fit) / summary(fit) and therefore show the new Representation: / Engine: lines. Full sweep deferred to v0.4.0 alongside the vignette deck restructure (per the v0.3.8 plan §12.3 ratification).
  • cran-comments.md: v0.3.8 bump + 3-NOTE-sub-item reframing.

Phase D test: (skip ledger + benchmark profiles).

  • New tools/skip_ledger.R parses every tests/testthat/test-*.R for skip() / skip_if_not() / skip_on_cran() / skip_if_not_installed() calls and classifies them against five reason classes (unavailable optional backend; CRAN/CI time budget; stress-only; external toolchain unavailable; deliberately deferred feature); writes inst/skip-ledger.md for users and reviewers.
  • Four named benchmark profiles under tools/profiles/: smoke.R (~30 s pure-R subset), release.R (5–10 min canonical release-ceremony gate), stress.R (sets FLEXYBAYES_RUN_STRESS=true; unblocks the greta MCMC posterior-equivalence tests), huge_n_probe.R (skeleton at v0.3.8; the actual N = 5e6 runs land at v0.4.0 per the trust-release gate).
  • tools/tally.R now refreshes inst/skip-ledger.md as its closing step.

Corrections

  • emit_gaussian_aggregated(): the aggregated INLA path now preserves the flexybayes_inla class label on the returned fit (c("flexybayes_aggregated", "flexybayes_inla", "flexybayes")). The previous shape dropped flexybayes_inla, so fb_as_draws_simple() dispatched to the greta extractor and crashed with “fitgretagretadraws is missing” – silently breaking triangulate(fit_g, fit_i) on the aggregated path. Class-invariant test_that() blocks in tests/testthat/test-emit-gaussian-aggregated.R cover both backend shapes. The greta path stays at the two-element c("flexybayes_aggregated", "flexybayes") (no flexybayes_greta class is introduced; fb_as_draws_simple.flexybayes is the greta extractor).
