  • tests/testthat/test-fb-brms.R:284 backend_decision() shape expectation updated from the 4-field ADR-0006 baseline to the 8-field ADR-0024 shape (backend / path / gate_checks / reason / preflight_summary / representation_plan / rejected_routes / routing_policy_version). The test silently failed under NOT_CRAN=true since the v0.3.6 close.

flexyBayes 0.3.7

Stage 5A – known-covariance input formats

vm() and ped() now accept user-supplied covariance carriers beyond the dense VV matrix. Three new formats activate in v0.3.7; two more reserve their input slots for v0.3.8 / v0.4.0:

  • Cholesky factor (greta backend):

    L <- t(chol(G))   # user pre-computes the lower-triangular factor
flexybayes(
  yield ~ env, random = ~ vm(geno, chol = L),
  data = dat, known_matrices = list(L = L),
  backend = "greta"
)

    Skips the t(chol(V)) step at fit time. Useful when LL is already available (e.g., from a prior pre-processing step that factorised a kinship matrix once and serialised the factor).

  • Sparse precision (greta + INLA backends):

    Q <- solve(G)     # or build sparse Q directly via ICAR / BYM2
flexybayes(
  y ~ 1, random = ~ vm(cell, precision = Q),
  data = dat, known_matrices = list(Q = Q),
  backend = "inla"
)

    Routes through INLA’s f(<var>_id, model = "generic0", Cmatrix = Q) interface (Rue & Held 2005, Gaussian Markov Random Fields; Lindgren et al. 2011) when backend = "inla". Order-of-magnitude memory win on large sparse problems (BYM2 spatial models, sparse-inverse pedigree relationship matrices). On greta the precision matrix densifies at fit time (as.matrix(solve(chol(Q)))); use INLA for the sparse-efficiency win.

  • Pedigree sparse-precision opt-in for ped():

    ped(animal, A_inv, use_sparse_precision = TRUE)

    When the user has already inverted the pedigree to A_inv = solve(A) (or pulled the sparse A−1A^{-1} directly from pedigreemm), this flag routes through the precision codepath without a redundant inversion. The user is responsible for the inversion at construction time; flexyBayes does not depend on pedigreemm or any other pedigree-graph library.

The dense VV path (vm(group, V = G)) is unchanged – byte-identical to v0.3.6. Existing fits saved as .rds reload without IR migration: the new cov_representation IR slot is additive, and legacy IRs default to format = "dense".

Two more formats reserve their input slots in v0.3.7 but refuse cleanly with forward-pointer messages: blocks = list(V1, V2, ...) defers to v0.3.8 with route_not_yet_emitted; low_rank_factor = + low_rank_scheme = "pca" defers to v0.4.0 (ADR 0027 approximation registry) with approximate_route_not_yet_registered. Reserving the input vocabulary now lets future releases ship without changing the vm() / ped() call shape.

Backend dispatch. With backend = "auto", INLA accepts vm/ped only when the precision representation is supplied; dense or chol inputs route to greta. With explicit backend = "inla", dense or chol inputs raise a structured lgm_gate refusal naming the actionable workaround (re-express as vm(group, precision = solve(V)), or route via backend = "greta"). The refusal text branches on the format to point the user at the right remedy.

Validation. Each format passes through a typed structural validator on the user-supplied matrix before the emit path runs:

  • chol must be square and lower-triangular (refusals chol_not_square, chol_not_triangular).
  • precision must be symmetric and positive-definite (refusals precision_not_symmetric, precision_not_positive_definite). The PD check uses base R chol() on the dense coercion; performance-grade sparse-PD probes land in v0.3.8.

Mutual exclusion across V / chol / precision / blocks / low_rank_factor is enforced at parse time with the vm_redundant_specification refusal.

Routing audit anchor. backend_decision(fit)$routing_policy_version bumps from "stage4_v1" to "stage5a_v1" (per ADR 0024) to record that INLA’s allowlist behaviour materially changed at v0.3.7.

flexyBayes 0.3.6

Stage 4 – backend routing trace + preflight metadata consumption

Two architectural additions complete the v0.2.6 -> v0.3.x dispatch story. The existing four-backend surface (greta / inla / brms-passthrough / gretaR-scaffold) now routes deliberately and reports its decisions reproducibly.

backend_decision(fit) gains four new fields. Every fit produced under v0.3.6 carries the existing four fields (backend / path / gate_checks / reason, per ADR 0006) plus:

  • preflight_summary – the .fb_preflight() return value when preflight ran (>1e5-row path); NULL on the small-data fast path by design.
  • representation_plan – a slim list of one entry per IR term: (term_id, representation_class, justification). Derived from preflight_summary; NULL when no preflight ran.
  • rejected_routes – a list of (backend, reason) pairs for the backends considered but not chosen. Empty for explicit user requests (policy bypassed). For backend = "auto", the list enumerates the non-chosen candidates from {greta, inla, gretaR} with per-backend reason codes.
  • routing_policy_version – the policy version that decided this fit’s dispatch (e.g., "stage4_v1"). Bumping this string is the audit-anchor for reproducibility – a fit produced under an older policy carries the older string.

Legacy fits (those that recorded the v0.2 / v0.3.5 four-field trace before v0.3.6 landed) read out via the accessor with NULL defaults on the four new fields; downstream code reading backend_decision(fit)$chosen_backend is unaffected.

lgm_gate(fb, preflight = NULL). The gate signature gains an optional second argument. When preflight is NULL (the v0.3.5 calling convention), the gate behaves exactly as today – 10 structural rules. When preflight is supplied, the gate runs an 11th rule, .lgm_check_memory_feasibility_inla(fb, preflight), that refuses when the INLA path’s projected memory exceeds the active ceiling. The Stage 4 ship is a single-multiplier approximation: INLA memory ~= 3x the indexed preflight total (the INLA dense intermediate inflation rule of thumb). Per-term estimators are queued for a follow-on release alongside the LGM-feasibility vignette; deferred at v0.3.6 close, deferred again at v0.3.7 close to keep the Stage 5A known-covariance work the focus, and deferred again at v0.3.8 close (audit hardening was prioritised). The multiplier is configurable via options(flexyBayes.inla_memory_multiplier = <value>). The new refusal reason code is memory_infeasibility_inla – distinct from the existing structural reason codes (fixed_term_type_inla / random_term_type_inla / rcov_term_type_inla from ADR 0017, the six original family / predictor / distributional / re_prior / latent_class / hyperparam_budget). The structural-vs-memory distinction is the central new piece of dispatch information – distinguishable from rejected_routes alone, without re-running the gate.

Routing-policy registry. The policy lives in .routing_policy_table(), a small data.frame in R/dispatch.R that encodes the (user_request, gate_outcome, preflight_outcome, inla_installed) tuple -> (chosen_backend, reason_code) mapping. This is the single source of truth: the dispatch logic queries the table via .resolve_routing() rather than re-deriving the decision from nested ifs. Changing the policy is a table-edit, not a control-flow surgery.

Approximate-scheme guard. Backend names carrying an approximate-scheme exactness label (e.g., "inla_pardiso_approximate", "variational_advi") now refuse at the entry function with approximate_route_not_yet_registered, pointing to ADR 0027 (the future approximation registry). The package’s identity rests on exactness labelling (per Stage 3A / ADR 0022); silently routing an approximate request would violate that contract.

Worked example – a memory-infeasible model on backend = "auto" now produces a trace like:

bd <- backend_decision(fit)
bd$backend                # "greta"
bd$path                   # "auto_lgm_refuse_memory"
bd$rejected_routes
# list(
#   list(backend = "inla",   reason = "memory_infeasibility_inla"),
#   list(backend = "gretaR", reason = "backend_not_activated")
# )
bd$routing_policy_version # "stage4_v1"

The decision is now reproducible from backend_decision(fit) alone, plus the policy version string. The reproducibility posture mirrors targets::tar_metadata() (Landau 2021), which captures the chosen execution plan plus the rejected alternatives + reasons on every pipeline run.

The vignette companion (flexyBayes-11-lgm-feasibility.Rmd.orig extension for the structural-vs-memory refusal distinction) is staged for v0.3.7 alongside the per-term INLA memory estimator.

flexyBayes 0.3.5

Stage 3B (file-output) – file-backed prediction + sample activation

Two additions to predict.flexybayes(newdata, ...) complete the Stage 3B scope opened at 0.3.4.

File-backed prediction output. Three new arguments – output_file, format, interop – route predict() to a disk-backed tabular output when output_file is supplied. The file carries point, lower, upper (95% posterior credible bounds) plus optional se.fit, plus the columns of newdata, under the format resolved by:

format = "auto" (default):
  if (interop)                        return "csv"
  if (N >= 1e6 && fst_available)      return "fst"
  if (N >= 1e6 && !fst_available)     return "rds"
  if (N <  1e6)                       return "rds"

format = "csv": always "csv" (no fst dependency)
format = "rds": always "rds" (no fst dependency)
format = "fst":
  if (fst_available)                  return "fst"
  else                                stop(structured_refusal_with_install_hint)

The fst path is 30-40x faster than rds at N >= 1e6 for essentially the same on-disk size (single-platform benchmark under benchmark_results/fst_stage3b_2026-05-23). fst is declared in Suggests with a >= 0.9.0 floor; predict(..., format = "fst") with fst not installed raises a structured refusal naming the install command and the format = "rds" override line. Refusing rather than silently falling back is consistent with the package’s broader no-silent-refusal posture. Pre-existing prediction grids are not overwritten: if output_file already exists, predict() raises a structured stop suggesting unlink() rather than overwriting silently.

The posterior intervals follow posterior expected-response quantile semantics (mirrors brms::posterior_epred(); Gelman et al. 2013, Bayesian Data Analysis, section 15.4 on linear-predictor posteriors): the linear predictor is evaluated under each retained posterior draw, the link inverse is applied per draw, and point / lower / upper are read off the rowwise mean and 2.5% / 97.5% quantiles. These are intervals on the expected response, not posterior-predictive intervals — they do not include residual observation noise. For full posterior-predictive intervals (observation noise included), route the in-memory draws through external tooling such as brms::posterior_predict() on a refit, or add a residual-noise draw per row using fit$sigma. Chunked vs unchunked file output is equivalent at floating-point precision; BLAS non-associativity at the matrix-size boundary introduces ULP-level differences (~2e-16) but no numerically meaningful drift.

allow_new_levels = "sample" is now active. The label was stable at 0.3.4; the implementation ships here. Unknown factor levels in newdata get a fresh Normal(0, tau_group) random-effect realisation layered onto the linear predictor per posterior draw (mirrors brms::posterior_epred(..., sample_new_levels = "gaussian")). Caller’s set.seed() controls reproducibility. The in-memory return reports the posterior-mean point estimate; the sampled-RE contribution averages toward zero across draws so the in-memory point estimate sits close to the population baseline – the file-backed return captures the proper per-row posterior interval reflecting sampled-RE uncertainty. INLA fits do not currently expose per-draw access and route to a structured refusal; an INLA draws adapter is queued for a future release.

Internals

  • New R/predict_file_output.R (.fst_available, .resolve_format, .predict_write_file, .predict_to_file).
  • New R/predict_posterior.R (.predict_per_draw, .predict_intervals, .predict_sample_re_for_unknowns, .predict_in_memory_sample).
  • R/predict_chunked.R – .predict_resolve_factors() drops the 0.3.4 deferred-stop on "sample"; the new branch tags unknown rows via attr(newdata, "sample_re_summary") for downstream per-draw consumption.
  • R/methods.R – predict.flexybayes() gains output_file, format, interop arguments and two new dispatch branches.

Test coverage

  • New tests/testthat/test-predict-file-output.R (16 blocks) covering the pure-path resolution table, the structured fst refusal, csv/rds/fst round-trip with factor preservation, chunked invariance, format = “auto” end-to-end with mocked fst availability, the interop branch, and overwrite refusal.
  • New tests/testthat/test-predict-sample-new-levels.R (7 blocks) covering active success on mixed known+unknown rows, caller-seed-driven non-determinism, posterior-interval variance scaling, backward-compat with legacy fits, deferred-stop removal confirmation, and the no-draws fit refusal.

Total test counts: PASS 1317 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 73 (0.3.4 baseline was 1262/0/73; +55 expectations across 22 new blocks).

flexyBayes 0.3.4

Stage 3B (core) – chunked indexed prediction + factor-dictionary handling

Three new pieces on the predict.flexybayes(newdata, ...) surface for prediction grids large enough to warrant chunked iteration and for cases where newdata carries factor levels not seen at fit time.

Dictionary-backed factor handling. Fits now carry a metadata- only <fb_dataset> descriptor (frozen factor-level dictionaries plus column-type cache) on fit$extras$fb_dataset. At predict(newdata) time, factor columns in newdata resolve against this dictionary instead of being re-derived from newdata. The change closes a latent silent-re-levelling bug where the v0.3.3 prediction path could permute a random-effect contribution under specific newdata orderings.

allow_new_levels = c("population", "sample", "refuse"). Policy for factor values in newdata that are not in the fit- time dictionary. "population" (default) coerces unknown-level rows to NA on the affected column and emits a warning naming the count; downstream prediction returns the population-level prediction for those rows. "refuse" raises a structured stop on the first unknown level, naming the column and (up to five) unknown values. "sample" (fresh random-effect draw per unknown level) is reserved at 0.3.4 – the label is stable but the implementation ships at 0.3.5 alongside the file-backed prediction output.

chunk_size argument. When supplied and nrow(newdata) > chunk_size, prediction iterates over chunks of the requested size and concatenates the per-chunk results. Default NULL preserves the single-pass behaviour. chunk_size is a wall-time / peak- memory knob – the numerical output is identical to the single- pass call. A typical setting at large newdata is chunk_size = 10000L.

The file-backed prediction output formats (format = c("auto", "csv", "rds", "fst") + output_file argument) ship together at 0.3.5; this release covers the in-memory prediction surface only.

flexyBayes 0.3.3

Stage 3A – Gaussian aggregated emit (greta path)

Completes the aggregated-gaussian path by activating the greta backend alongside INLA. fb_brms(..., backend = "greta", aggregate = TRUE) and flexybayes(..., backend = "greta", aggregate = TRUE) now route through the same sufficient-statistics emit as the INLA path. The greta implementation factorises the cell-mean weighted gaussian observation against a gamma observation on the within-cell sum of squares; together these recover the per-row gaussian log- likelihood exactly (the algebraic identity proof is in Searle, Casella & McCulloch (1992) Variance Components §3). On a fixed- seed synthetic dataset with N = 800, J = 20, the aggregated greta posterior recovers a known (beta, sigma, tau) triple within MC tolerance; the backend-fidelity check is shipped as a stress-gated test (FLEXYBAYES_RUN_STRESS=true).

Known caveat. The aggregated INLA path still uses an explicit loggamma(1, 5e-5) precision prior on random-intercept terms when the user has not supplied a prior via prior = fb_prior(...), for the data-scale-stability reason in the 0.3.2 caveat. Unifying the default-prior behaviour across per-row and aggregated paths remains queued. The greta aggregated path follows the same default prior shape (sd-scale) as the per-row greta path; matched-prior comparisons within greta are therefore consistent without extra configuration.

Heterogeneous residual. at(f):units on greta now flows through the aggregated path end-to-end (when f is in the cell key). The multi-likelihood INLA stack required for the same on the INLA aggregated path remains queued.

flexyBayes 0.3.2

Stage 3A – Gaussian aggregated emit (INLA path)

Wires the sufficient-statistics aggregation foundation (introduced in 0.3.0 as <fb_aggregated> + <fb_aggregation_plan>) into the live dispatch path. Gaussian-identity LMMs whose linear predictor is cell-constant – fixed numeric / factor effects plus random intercepts on factor groupings – now have an aggregated emit path that fits the same posterior on per-cell sufficient statistics rather than per-observation likelihood contributions. The aggregated log-likelihood is the algebraic identity of the per-row form (no approximation; see Searle, Casella & McCulloch (1992) Variance Components §3 and Bates et al. (2015) §3 on the profiled-deviance shortcut); the bit-exact equivalence is gated by a property-based test in tests/testthat/test-aggregate-gaussian.R.

API. A new aggregate = c("auto", TRUE, FALSE) argument joins flexybayes() and fb_brms(). The default "auto" consults the plan and silently routes through the aggregated emit when the IR is in scope and compression is productive (K/N <= 0.5); falls through to the per-row path when out of scope. TRUE forces aggregation – raises a structured refusal naming the plan’s reason code when ineligible. FALSE skips the gate entirely.

Exactness field. Every flexybayes fit now carries an $exactness slot. Per-row paths populate it as "exact"; aggregated paths populate it as "aggregated_exact". The dispatch trace’s path slot reads "aggregated_gaussian" on aggregated fits. summary() and a new print.flexybayes_aggregated() / summary.flexybayes_aggregated() surface the field plus a compression-ratio line when N/K >= 2 (suppressed on smaller datasets to avoid misleading claims).

Backend coverage at 0.3.2. INLA-backed aggregation is shipped end-to-end (cell-mean weighted gaussian + a custom precision-prior expression that absorbs the within-cell sum-of-squares correction; the algebra is documented in the file header). Greta-backed aggregation is deferred to a follow-on – the algebraic pattern (cell-mean weighted gaussian plus a gamma observation on the within-cell SS) is viable, but the package wiring needs a codegen-without-runtime-parse workaround for an R S3 dispatch context-sensitivity that surfaces only inside the package namespace. aggregate = TRUE on backend = "greta" refuses cleanly with a deferred-feature message; aggregate = "auto" on greta silently falls through to the per-row path.

Heterogeneous residual. at(f):units is supported on the aggregated path when f is a cell-key term (so each cell has a single residual variance). When the residual factor is not a cell key the per-row / per-cell algebraic identity breaks and the emit refuses with a structured heterogeneous_residual_factor_not_in_- cell_key reason code.

Known caveat. The aggregated INLA path uses an explicit loggamma(1, 5e-5) precision prior on random-intercept terms when the user has not supplied a prior via prior = fb_prior(...), because INLA’s data-scale-dependent default would otherwise produce different effective priors on the per-row and aggregated data scales. Matched-prior comparisons between per-row and aggregated paths therefore require either passing an explicit fb_prior() or accepting that the residual / random-intercept posteriors will differ on tail behaviour. The fixed-effect posteriors remain bit-exactly equivalent under the algebraic identity. Unifying the per-row default-prior behaviour with the aggregated path is queued for a follow-on.

flexyBayes 0.3.1

Trust Pass – preflight + aggregation honesty hardening

A focused three-phase pass on the public API’s honesty contract, spanning the preflight layer, the aggregation taxonomy, and the public-facing metadata. Closes a deep review of the v0.3.0.9000 development tip end-to-end. No user-facing API signature changes; every revision tightens behaviour the package already promised.

Trust bugs. A session-level options(flexyBayes.review_code_default = TRUE) no longer slips past the unsupported-backend refusal on backend = "inla" / "auto" for either flexybayes() or fb_brms() – option resolution now runs before the backend guard. The preflight refusal headline no longer claims “the design exceeds the active memory ceiling” when the refusal is actually representation_unknown_for_preflight; the headline now branches on the reason code so an unknown-representation refusal does not falsely send the user down the ceiling-override path.

Preflight taxonomy. Structured-covariance random terms are split into known-indexed forms (vm, ped, ar1, ar1_spatial) that keep the tested heuristic estimator, and everything else (at, us, fa, at_simple, us_gxe, fa_gxe, vm_gxe, …) that now routes to representation_unknown_for_preflight rather than silently under-estimating the design memory at large N. The previous “single level” fallback in .preflight_term_level_count() was replaced with NA_integer_; every consumer branch (structured-cov, random intercept, uncorrelated random slope, fixed factor, factor :numeric interaction) now treats an unresolvable level count as the signal to escalate to an unknown-representation refusal.

Aggregation refusal codes. The Stage 3A out-of-scope taxonomy was renamed and aligned across the two emitters that report it: .assert_aggregate_in_scope() (the runtime gate) and .fb_aggregation_plan() (the model-level planner) now produce the same reason code for the same model. The previous catch-all random_slope_in_scope is replaced by three positively-named codes (random_slope_not_aggregatable, structured_random_not_aggregatable, smooth_term_not_aggregatable); the planner’s compression_data_dependent is renamed continuous_cell_key_data_dependent for clarity.

Public-facing metadata. The codemeta.json version field, the cran-comments.md build description, SECURITY.md, SUPPORT.md, and the README’s review_code support row are all refreshed for the 0.3.x line. API_STABILITY.md splits the structured-covariance default-priors row by actual implemented behaviour (vm/ped on the uniform-on-SD default; at/us/fa/ar1/spl on the legacy lognormal). CONTRIBUTING.md documents the source-directory R CMD check footgun and recommends the build-then-check workflow.

The AAGI-AUS GitHub URL declared in DESCRIPTION is the agreed forward destination; until the upstream repository rename ships, the CRAN-incoming feasibility check raises a sub-NOTE for the URL. cran-comments.md itemises this and the other structural NOTE sub-items in full.

Test coverage

PASS 1187 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 72 on tools/tally.R (was 1151/0/72 at the deep-review baseline; +36 expectations across the Trust Pass). 9 new test_that blocks pin the structured-covariance preflight split and the renamed aggregation taxonomy; 8 ordered cases pin the review_code option-default ordering across both formula verbs.

flexyBayes 0.3.0.9000

Stage 3A foundation – exact Gaussian aggregation via sufficient statistics

Internal .fb_aggregate_gaussian() collapses a per-row Gaussian-identity mixed model into one row per cell, where a cell is the maximal subset of observations sharing the same linear-predictor value. Three sufficient statistics per cell (n_k, S1_k = sum(y), S2_k = sum(y^2)) carry all the information the Gaussian-identity log-likelihood needs.

The implementation is foundation-only at this release: the algebraic correctness gate landed, the backend emit path is not yet wired. A property-based test draws twenty random in-scope intermediate representations across three N scales (100, 500, 2000) with random coefficients and confirms that the aggregated log-likelihood matches the raw per-row form to relative error below 1e-12 in every case. The biased cell-mean shortcut is exposed only so the same test can confirm a regression would be caught.

The scope envelope refuses (typed condition flexybayes_aggregate_out_of_scope) on: non-Gaussian family, non-identity link, smooth fixed-effect term, or any random slope – all of which break the cell-constant linear predictor.

Internal-only at v0.3.0.9000; surfaces user-facing in v0.3.2 alongside the greta / INLA aggregated emit path and the $exactness slot.

Stage 3A foundation – memory shape correction + model-level plan

Two follow-up changes to the Stage 3A foundation surfaced by the 2026-05-23 audit:

  • <fb_aggregated>$design_matrix (the full N x p per-row design matrix) is replaced by $cell_design (the K x p per-cell form). The aggregated emit path only needs the per-cell linear predictor; carrying the per-row matrix defeated the compression contract at large N and was not an implementation shape compatible with the 10M-100M-row roadmap. Per-row equivalence verification (the bit-exact log-likelihood gate) now rebuilds the per-row design locally via stats::model.matrix().

  • New internal .fb_aggregation_plan() returning a model-level <fb_aggregation_plan> with seven slots: eligible, reason_codes, cell_key_terms, requires_materialisation, K_est, N, compression_est. The plan reads only IR + dataset metadata; no design materialised. .fb_preflight() attaches the plan to its result for diagnostic visibility. The plan is informational at v0.3.0.9000: the per-term aggregated_likelihood_candidate flag remains the dispatcher contract through v0.3.1. In v0.3.2 the plan supersedes per-term flags as the dispatch input when the aggregated emit path lands.

    Productivity threshold: K_est / N <= 0.5 (at least 2:1 compression expected from metadata). Below the threshold the plan reports eligible = TRUE; above it reports reason_codes = "compression_unproductive". Continuous fixed terms make the cell count data-dependent (cannot estimate from metadata) and the plan reports reason_codes = "compression_data_dependent".

Preflight hardening – smooth/spline estimators + unknown-term refusal

The Stage 2 preflight layer now characterises every term class the asreml and brms parsers can emit. Five new branches:

  • Mgcv smooth terms (s(x), smooth_mgcv in the IR) on either side of the formula: dense N x k basis estimate using the resolved term$k from mgcv::smoothCon(). Previously parser-emitted smooths fell through to a single-column estimate – a factor-of-k under-estimate that could let a large smooth model pass preflight when the actual basis exceeded the ceiling.
  • P-spline terms (spl(x)): dense N x df basis with df = 8 matching the codegen default.
  • Factor:factor interactions: dense treatment-coded N x (prod(L) - 1) estimate; the audit-named high-cardinality scary case.
  • Factor:continuous interactions (ADR 0019 indexed slope): integer index column + continuous column + (L - 1) per-level slope coefficients.
  • Polynomial terms (pol(x, d)): dense N x d basis.

The fixed and random fallthrough branches no longer record a single-dense-column estimate framed as “conservative lower bound” – a lower bound is the opposite of conservative for a refusal gate. Unrecognised term classes now flag the per-term entry with unknown_representation = TRUE and the top-level preflight returns a typed flexybayes_preflight_refusal with reason_code = "representation_unknown_for_preflight" carrying the binding term label. Structured-covariance random terms (vm, ped, fa, us, at, ar1, nested, etc.) remain estimated via the indexed-representation heuristic and are now labelled representation_class = "indexed_structured_estimate" with a header note that production fits at large N should set memory_ceiling_gb explicitly rather than relying on the default.

Behaviour change – default RAM fraction lowered from 80% to 60%

The default design-memory ceiling is now 60% of system RAM (was 80%). This is conservative for shared workstations, CI runners, and interactive laptops where the user expects the rest of the machine to remain responsive under load. A new global option flexyBayes.preflight_ram_fraction exposes the fraction for per-host tuning:

options(flexyBayes.preflight_ram_fraction = 0.5)   # tighter
options(flexyBayes.preflight_ram_fraction = 0.9)   # looser, single-user host

The fraction is validated as (0, 1]. The 8 GiB fallback (used when neither the benchmarkme nor the memuse RAM probe is installed) is unaffected – the fallback is already a conservative absolute floor.

flexyBayes 0.3.0

Stage 2 design-memory preflight

flexyBayes now estimates the design-representation memory of a model upstream of the backend dispatch and refuses with a structured diagnostic when the estimate exceeds an active ceiling. The aim is to replace the v0.2 silent-allocation antipattern (Error: cannot allocate vector of size 3.2 Gb from model.matrix() mid-fit) with an explicit, per-term refusal that names the binding term and a numeric override.

The default ceiling is 80% of system RAM, probed via benchmarkme or memuse when either is installed; otherwise an 8 GiB fallback applies. Users can set a stricter cap via the global option flexyBayes.preflight_ceiling_gb (e.g. on shared hosts where the full RAM should not be claimed for a single fit).

The check runs only on fits with n_rows >= 1e5 so the v0.2 user surface is unchanged at small scales. On larger fits the check reads only n_rows, factor-level counts, and column types – no row-wise data scan – so the runtime is O(terms) regardless of n_rows. A 1e8-row metadata-only check completes in milliseconds on the development laptop.

The refusal is a typed condition flexybayes_preflight_refusal carrying the binding term name, its byte estimate, the active ceiling, and a suggested override. On flexybayes(..., review_code = TRUE) and fb_brms(..., review_code = TRUE) the resulting <flexybayes_review> token now carries a $preflight slot; the preflight summary appears in print(rev) above the cat_code() prompt.

The aggregated_likelihood_candidate flag on each per-term entry is a forward-looking promise to the gaussian-identity aggregated backend path; the flag has no runtime effect at v0.3.0 (no aggregation runs yet) but is consumed by later stages.

flexyBayes 0.2.6

Correctness fix – factor:continuous interaction (ADR 0019)

flexybayes(y ~ x * f, data = ...) where f is a factor and x is numeric previously emitted the interaction term using a coefficient broadcast that did not match base R’s treatment-coded model matrix – producing posterior estimates that disagreed with lme4::lmer by more than three standard deviations on simulated data. The fix emits the interaction as a treatment-coded indexed slope: the reference level’s slope is fixed to zero; the L-1 non- reference levels carry their own slope deviations sampled from the prior, indexed back to the observation vector via the factor’s level codes. Posterior estimates now match lme4::lmer within MCMC tolerance and the linear-predictor equality eta_flexybayes == model.matrix(~ f * x) %*% beta holds at tolerance 1e-10 for any compatible coefficient vector.

The new term class factor_numeric_interaction registers the canonical-name family slope_<f>_<x>[<level>] per non-reference level for both the greta and brms backends. The dispatch trace records which emit branch fired via fit$extras$parse_info$factor_continuous_emit ("option_c" for the greta-native concatenation idiom; "option_d" for the per- observation lookup-vector fallback gated on options(flexyBayes.force_option_d = TRUE)).

Unsupported contrast types (contr.helmert, contr.sdif, contr.sum, ordered factors, user-supplied custom contrast matrices) refuse at ingest with a structured flexybayes_contrast_unsupported condition carrying contrast, factor_name, and deferral_target slots; the message points at the v0.3 representation IR for general contrast support.

The INLA mapper for the new term class registers only after a three-arbitrator verification test (INLA vs greta vs lme4::lmer) passes on the host; on hosts where INLA verification cannot complete the gate refuses INLA dispatch with a v0.3 deferral message rather than silently shipping an unverified translation.

Feature – uncorrelated random slopes (x || g) (ADR 0020)

fb_brms(y ~ x + (x || g), ...) now parses and emits the uncorrelated random-effect form – in lme4 / brms semantics each level of g carries an independent intercept deviation AND an independent slope deviation, both drawn from their own univariate- normal priors (no correlation parameter shared between intercept and slope). The explicit (1 + x || g) shape is equivalent; (0 + x || g) suppresses the intercept block, yielding a slope- only random effect. The correlated form (x | g) continues to refuse with a v0.3 deferral message pointing to ADR 0025 (Stage 5A known-covariance inputs), which will admit the user- supplied Cholesky factor that makes the correlated form tractable; the refusal raises a typed condition (flexybayes_correlated_slope_unsupported) carrying grouping_factor, slope_variable, deferral_target, and workaround slots so downstream tooling can pattern-match.

Canonical-name family sd_<x>_<g> registered on the greta + brms backends – the brms-side sd_<g>__<x> parameter (brms’s double-underscore Stan convention) maps to the canonical sd_<x>_<g>. INLA mapping is gated by a three-arbitrator verification test (INLA vs greta vs lme4) on a simple fixture following the §3.4 verification policy in plan-indexing-bigdata-merged-2026-05-23-v2.md; until the verification artefact records pass, the INLA backend refuses (x || g) with a v0.3 deferral message naming backend = "greta" as the workaround. Triangulation between greta and brms on (x || g) fits agrees on slope-variance posteriors within W_1 <= 0.20 * tau_true (the loosened envelope per merged-v2 §5.6 risk 3 – slope-variance posteriors are intrinsically less identified than intercept-variance ones at modest J).

Representation benchmarks (Stage 1C per merged-v2 plan section 4.2.3)

The benchmark harness gains three new rows per term class: generated_code_size_bytes, pre_fit_object_size_bytes, and code_generation_time_sec. Snapshot tests assert that the greta fit-time codegen path does not call model.matrix() for supported indexed term classes – the indexed-emit path replaces the dense matrix at any n, so generated code size stays nearly constant in n.

Benchmark filename rename: tools/benchmark_flexyBayes_0.2.5.R -> tools/benchmark_flexyBayes.R (version stamp dropped; the harness runs against whichever version is installed, and names its output directory accordingly at run time).

flexyBayes 0.2.5.9000

Correctness fix – predict(newdata) on smooths (ADR 0018)

predict.flexybayes(..., newdata = ...) on fits containing one or more s() smooth terms now uses retained mgcv Smooth objects via mgcv::PredictMat(), restoring correctness on newdata containing x values inside or near the training range. Previously the basis was implicitly re-derived from newdata via stats::model.matrix(), producing correct-by-coincidence values inside the training range and silently wrong values near or beyond. The fix retains the mgcv::smoothCon() output on the IR (internal slot random_terms[[i]]$smooth_obj) and threads it via extras$parse_info$smooths. fb_brms(backend = "brms") and fb_greta() are exempt – both already correct.

A correctness refusal fires on legacy fits saved before this fix: re-fit on the current version to enable predict(newdata).

Code-size fix – smooth emit literal-matrix storage

The greta emit path for s() smooths no longer inlines the n-row basis matrix as a literal in the generated code. The basis is bound into the model environment as B_s_<varname> and the emitted code references as_data(B_s_<varname>) instead. nchar(return_code(fit)) for s(x) at n = 10000 dropped from ~10 MB to under 10 kB.

Gate truth = emit truth (ADR 0017)

lgm_gate(fb) == accept is now a sufficient condition for the INLA emit path to succeed structurally. Three new gate rules (fixed_term_type_inla, random_term_type_inla, rcov_term_type_inla) fold the prior emit-time refusal sites into lgm_gate() so users see refusals before the INLA machinery is invoked. backend = "auto" no longer carries a separate emit-time fall-back path; dispatch trace’s auto-non-LGM path is uniformly "auto_lgm_refuse".

Visual-regression test tier upgraded (AMBITION_STAGE §1.1)

The vdiffr SVG-snapshot tests in test-plot-vdiffr.R (which had been skipped unconditionally due to MCMC-float-drift fragility) are replaced with numerical snapshots on the plotted data structure. Equivalent coverage for “did the plot get built correctly” without the SVG-diff fragility.

Structured-cov default priors – vm() + ped() now uniform-on-SD

.default_uniform_prior() (extending ADR 0004) now fires on vm() and ped() random-term inputs, closing the documented inconsistency where simple/ide/id RE SDs defaulted to uniform-on-SD while vm/ped fell back to legacy lognormal. The other structured forms (at, us, fa, ar1) remain on the legacy default for now.

flexyBayes 0.2.0 (development)

Four-verb API

flexyBayes exposes four user-facing entry points covering the formula-grammar × backend-ambition cross-product:

Verb Grammar Backend choices Use when
flexybayes() ASReml (fixed / random / rcov) greta, inla, auto ASReml syntax; agricultural / variance-component workflows.
fb_brms() brms / lme4 (y ~ x + (1 | g)) greta, inla, brms, auto brms or lme4 syntax; Stan passthrough on backend = "brms".
fb_greta() direct greta model graph greta Expert escape hatch; supplies a pre-built greta model.
triangulate() n/a n/a Pairwise cross-engine posterior comparison.

fb() remains as a literal alias for flexybayes().

Dispatch trace

Every fit records a structured backend_decision() describing which backend ran and why:

fit <- flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ geno, data = trial)
backend_decision(fit)
#> $backend     "greta"
#> $path        "auto_inla_refuse"
#> $gate_checks <list of lgm_gate rules + pass/fail>
#> $reason      "lgm_gate refused at check `hyperparam_budget`."

backend = "auto" runs lgm_gate() and routes to INLA on acceptance, otherwise to greta. auto never routes to Stan — brms’s first-call Stan compile (typically 30–60 s) is incompatible with the auto-fast- path promise; Stan is opt-in only via explicit backend = "brms" on fb_brms().

Stan passthrough on fb_brms(backend = "brms")

fb_brms() builds the flexyBayes intermediate representation (IR), translates the prior, hands off to brms::brm(), and wraps the returned brmsfit in a c("flexybayes_brms", "flexybayes") subclass. The live brmsfit is exposed on the $brms slot so brms’s own posterior tooling (loo(), posterior_predict(), bayes_factor()) remains directly available.

fit_s <- fb_brms(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject),
                 data = sleepstudy, backend = "brms")
fit_g <- fb_brms(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject),
                 data = sleepstudy, backend = "greta")
triangulate(fit_s, fit_g)

review_code = TRUE on the Stan path returns Stan source via brms::make_stancode() — compile-free inspection before any Stan compilation fires.

Cross-engine triangulation

triangulate(fit_a, fit_b) computes mean difference, SD ratio, tail drift, Wasserstein-1, and R-hat-on-means on every parameter the two fits have in common. Canonical-name resolution (see below) means the caller usually does not need to pass a name_map.

fit_g <- flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ geno, data = trial,
                    backend = "greta")
fit_i <- flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ geno, data = trial,
                    backend = "inla")
triangulate(fit_g, fit_i)
#> Common parameters: 5
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   parameter        mean_diff sd_ratio tail_drift wasserstein_1 rhat_means
#>   <chr>                <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)        -0.041   0.997      0.012         0.041     1.002
#> ...

canonical_names() registry

Each backend names parameters differently (greta’s sigma_g, INLA’s Precision for g on the precision scale, brms’s sd_g__Intercept, etc.). canonical_names() resolves backend-native names to a single canonical name and applies the appropriate scale transform — most visibly, INLA’s precision draws are flipped to the SD scale before comparison.

canonical_names(fit_i)
#>   native                canonical    transform
#>   "(Intercept)"         "(Intercept)" identity
#>   "Precision for g"     "sd_g"        1/sqrt(.)
#>   "Precision for the Gaussian observations" "sigma" 1/sqrt(.)

triangulate() uses the registry to align parameters before computing metrics.

prior_summary() accessor

A new exported S3 generic surfaces the resolved priors used to fit the model. The summary distinguishes three resolution paths:

  • auto-default — bounded uniform on SD per Gelman (2006); fires when neither a user fb_prior() nor a legacy prior_vc_sd scalar is supplied.
  • user-supplied — the fb_prior() object the caller passed via the prior argument.
  • legacy-scalar — the prior_fixed_sd / prior_vc_sd bridge, preserved verbatim when prior_vc_sd is passed explicitly.
fit <- flexybayes(Reaction ~ Days, random = ~ Subject,
                  data = sleepstudy)
prior_summary(fit)
#> <prior_summary>  backend = greta
#>   Source: auto-default bounded uniform on SD (Gelman 2006)
#>     Upper bound U = 282.7
#>     Scale basis    = 5 * sd(Reaction)

On fb_greta() fits the summary is flagged declaration_only = TRUE because flexyBayes does not re-prior the user-built greta graph; the prior records what the user declared the model encodes.

review_code = TRUE workflow

A new optional argument on flexybayes(), fb_brms(), and fb_greta() lets users inspect the generated backend code before any sampling fires, then advance into the fit when ready:

rev <- flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ geno, data = trial,
                  review_code = TRUE)
rev                  # two-line summary: backend + IR dimensions
cat_code(rev)        # emit the generated greta (or Stan) code
fit <- proceed(rev)  # fit; a second proceed(rev) returns the cache

The returned <flexybayes_review> object carries the generated code, the parsed IR, the resolved prior, the captured call, and a snapshot of .Random.seed. The seed snapshot is restored on proceed() entry so a direct call and a review-then-proceed pair reproduce the same R-RNG state.

review_code = TRUE and return_code = TRUE (the older code-string-only option) are mutually exclusive. Default is FALSE; session-level override via options(flexyBayes.review_code_default = TRUE).

Prior contract

Auto-default (no prior and no prior_vc_sd supplied):

Target Default Notes
Residual sigma (Gaussian / identity link) uniform(0, 5 * sd(y)) Gelman 2006
Residual sigma (log link) uniform(0, 5 * sd(log(y + 0.5))) Gelman 2006
Residual sigma (logit link) uniform(0, 5) Gelman 2006
sd(group) for simple / ide / id terms matched to residual by family Gelman 2006
Fixed-effect coefficients normal(0, prior_fixed_sd), prior_fixed_sd = 100 Gelman 2006

Structured-covariance random terms (vm, ped, at, us, fa, ar1) currently fall back to the legacy lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) default; per-form uniform defaults are scheduled for v0.2.5.

The PC prior remains a first-class explicit option via fb_prior(sigma ~ pc(upper = U, prob = p)) and is the cross-engine interlingua (Simpson et al. 2017) for translation across greta / INLA / brms.

The prior_fixed_sd default was raised from 10 to 100 in this cycle; the previous value was too tight for responses on the natural data scale (e.g., sleepstudy$Reaction with mean ≈ 298 ms) and induced a substantial intercept bias against the REML reference.

fb_prior() accepts the targets sigma, sd(group), b(name), cor(group), smooth(var), and the families pc, normal, student_t, half_normal, half_cauchy, cauchy, gamma, exponential, lkj, uniform.

LGM feasibility filter

lgm_gate(fb) runs a structural feasibility check on the parsed IR before INLA dispatch. The filter returns either an acceptance or an lgm_refusal object carrying every rule that failed, the diagnostic, the suggested re-route (backend = "brms" via fb_brms() for the Stan passthrough; greta for the broader flexyBayes formula path), and a two-key-armed override path.

The structural refusals currently live in two places (the gate plus emit_inla()); folding the emit-time refusals into the gate is the ADR 0017 v0.2.5 work.

gretaR slot

A dormant scaffold for the gretaR backend is registered: gretaR_status() reports activated = FALSE and explains the activation procedure. The four touch-points (match.arg extension, canonical-name mapper, dispatch branch, status helper) are in place so v0.3 activation reduces to a single short patch plus the emit_gretaR.R body — once the gretaR package goes public and audit-clean.

  1. Getting started · 2. ASReml-shaped formulas · 3. Foundational regression · 4. Hierarchical models · 5. Structured covariance ·
  2. Priors and regularisation · 7. METs and genomic selection ·
  3. Downstream analysis · 9. Spatio-temporal models · 10. Cross- engine triangulation · 11. LGM feasibility filter · 12. Backend internals.

Heavy MCMC vignettes use a .Rmd.orig precompile pattern (vignettes/_precompile.R); the .Rmd that ships in the package tarball is the pre-evaluated static output.
